detection_pack.sigma:
title: APEX - Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plug — Authentication Bypass
id: apex-authbypass-50da2acb
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects authentication bypass exploitation for CVE-2026-15981. Covers admin path access, token manipulation, forced browsing, and unexpected successful authentication after failure patterns.
  Generated by CYBERDUDEBIVASH SENTINEL APEX v184.0
references:
    - https://intel.cyberdudebivash.com
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15981
author: CYBERDUDEBIVASH SENTINEL APEX
date: 2026/10/15
tags:
    - attack.credential_access
    - attack.t1078
    - attack.t1110
    - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  admin_direct_access_200:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/admin'
      - '/administrator'
      - '/manage'
      - '/dashboard'
      - '/console'
      - '/actuator'
      - '/api/admin'
    sc-status: 200
    cs-method: 'GET'
  jwt_none_algorithm:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0'
      - 'eyJhbGciOiAibm9uZSJ9'
  repeated_auth_failure_then_success:
    keywords:
      - '401 401 401 200'
      - 'Invalid credentials'
  condition: admin_direct_access_200 or jwt_none_algorithm
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate admin panel access from known IP addresses
  - Monitoring systems performing health checks on admin endpoints
level: high
detection_pack.spl:
| comment "Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plug | CVE-2026-15981 | APEX v184.0"

index=network OR index=proxy earliest=-24h
| eval threat_match = if(match(_raw, "(?i)(CVE\-2026\-15981)"), 1, 0)
| where threat_match=1
| eval rule="APEX-CVE-2026-15981", severity="HIGH"
| stats count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen by src_ip, dest_host, rule, severity
| convert timeformat="%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort -count
detection_pack.yara:
rule APEX_CVE_2026_15981__AUTH_BYPASS {
    meta:
        description   = "APEX detection: Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plugin Were Ex"
        cve           = "CVE-2026-15981"
        vuln_class    = "AUTH_BYPASS"
        author        = "CYBERDUDEBIVASH SENTINEL APEX v184.0"
        date          = "2026-10-15"
        reference     = "https://intel.cyberdudebivash.com"
        severity      = "high"
        mitre_attack  = "T1190"
    strings:
        $cve_ref = "CVE-2026-15981" ascii wide nocase  // CVE reference — narrow with observed payload
    condition:
        2 of them
}
detection_pack.elastic_lucene:
// Elastic Lucene: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda
("<indicator>") AND @timestamp:[now-30d TO now]
detection_pack.qradar_aql:
/* QRadar AQL: Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plug | intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda */
SELECT DATEFORMAT(devicetime,'YYYY-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') AS EventTime,
  sourceip, destinationip, username, LOGSOURCENAME(logsourceid) AS Source,

  desc: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda - TT1078 | TT1110
  condition: spawned_process and (proc.cmdline contains "<indicator>")

detection_pack.osquery:
-- OSQuery: Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plug | intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda
SELECT pid, name, cmdline, path, parent, uid
FROM processes
WHERE (cmdline LIKE '%indicator%');

retro_hunt.spl_splunk:
| comment "RETRO-HUNT: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda | Two CVSS 9.8 Auth Bypasses in miniOrange SAML WordPress Plug | Techniques: T1078 T1190"
index=* earliest=-90d latest=now
(
    ("<ip_indicator>")
    OR ("<domain_indicator>")
    OR ("<hash_indicator>")
)
| eval hunt_advisory="intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda"
| eval hunt_techniques="T1078 T1190"
| eval hunt_ts=strftime(_time, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| eval indicator_type=case(
    match(_raw, "(x.x.x.x"), "IP",
    match(_raw, "(domain"), "Domain",
    match(_raw, "(hash"), "Hash",
    1==1, "Unknown"
  )
| stats count AS hits,
    min(_time) AS first_seen,
    max(_time) AS last_seen,
    dc(host) AS affected_hosts,
    values(sourcetype) AS sources
    BY hunt_advisory, indicator_type, host
| where hits > 0
| eval first_seen=strftime(first_seen,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
       last_seen=strftime(last_seen,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| sort - hits
retro_hunt.qradar_aql:
/* RETRO-HUNT AQL: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda | Lookback: 90d */
SELECT
    DATEFORMAT(devicetime,'YYYY-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') AS EventTime,
    sourceip, destinationip, destinationhostname,
    username, "Application", "Event Category",
    LOGSOURCENAME(logsourceid) AS LogSource,
    QIDNAME(qid) AS EventName,
    'intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda' AS HuntAdvisoryID
FROM events
WHERE (
    destinationip IN ('<ip>')
    OR sourceip IN ('<ip>')
    OR destinationhostname IN ('<domain>')
    OR LOOKUPHOSTNAME(destinationip) IN ('<domain>')
)
AND devicetime > (NOW() - 7776000)
ORDER BY devicetime DESC
LIMIT 10000
START '90d ago'
STOP 'now'
retro_hunt.crowdstrike_eql:
/* RETRO-HUNT CrowdStrike Event Query: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda | Techniques: T1078, T1190 */
#type=ProcessRollup2 | head 1000
| eval hunt_id="intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda"
| search (sha256 = "<hash>") OR (DomainName = "<domain>")
| stats count by HostName, FileName, CommandLine, UserSid, TimeStamp
| sort count desc
retro_hunt.generic_sql:
/* RETRO-HUNT Generic SQL: intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda | Lookback: 90d */
/* Compatible with: Splunk Data Lake, Snowflake, BigQuery, Azure Data Explorer */
SELECT
    event_timestamp,
    host_name,
    source_ip,
    destination_ip,
    destination_domain,
    file_hash_sha256,
    process_name,
    process_command_line,
    user_name,
    'intel--be8a7f1af345e21243dabfda' AS hunt_advisory_id
FROM security_events
WHERE event_timestamp > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '90 days'
  AND (
    destination_ip IN ('<ip>')
    OR source_ip IN ('<ip>')
    OR destination_domain IN ('<domain>')
    OR file_hash_sha256 IN ('<hash>')
  )
ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 50000;
